files.name: TokenEndpoint.java

notes.4: Handles a request whose body is a serialized Java object.
notes.5: Wraps the request body in an ObjectInputStream.
notes.6: Reconstructs an object graph from the bytes — instantiating whatever classes the stream specifies.
notes.7: Passes the result on for processing.

options.label: `readObject` reconstructs arbitrary serializable classes and runs their callbacks (readObject/readResolve/finalize), so a crafted stream drives a gadget chain of classes on the classpath to execute code
`readObject` blocks until the whole body arrives, enabling a slow-read DoS
options.whyWrong: A DoS is minor next to the remote code execution this allows.

options.label: Casting `token` to a concrete type later may throw ClassCastException
options.whyWrong: By the time any cast runs, the gadget has already executed during readObject.

options.label: Wrap readObject in try/catch and return null on error
options.whyWrong: The gadget executes during readObject; catching the exception afterward doesn't prevent it.

options.label: Don't deserialize untrusted input — use a data format (e.g. JSON) or enforce a strict class allowlist via ObjectInputFilter
Run the handler under a restricted OS user
options.whyWrong: Dropping privileges limits blast radius but still allows code execution as that user; the deserialization sink is unchanged.

source.attribution: SourceReadle original (Java ObjectInputStream deserialization; ysoserial / FoxGlove 2015 research)

training.exploit: If a library with a known gadget chain (e.g. Apache Commons Collections) is on the classpath, generate a payload with a tool like ysoserial and POST it as the request body. When `readObject` deserializes it, the chain's callbacks run and execute an attacker command — unauthenticated remote code execution, no valid token required.

hints.line: The sink turns posted bytes into live Java objects.
hints.why: What runs while Java reconstructs a serialized object graph?
hints.fix: Don't native-deserialize untrusted input; use data-only parsing.

writeup.summary: `ObjectInputStream.readObject` reconstructs whatever classes the byte stream names and invokes their serialization callbacks, so an attacker who can POST bytes drives a 'gadget chain' of classes already on the classpath (famously Apache Commons Collections) to execute code — before any application logic runs. The robust fix is to not native-deserialize untrusted input at all: use a data-only format like JSON, or, if Java serialization is unavoidable, install a strict `ObjectInputFilter` allowlist. Try/catch and privilege-dropping don't stop the gadget from firing.
